beats: A man has sat in the same London university for over a hundred and seventy years, and he's been dead the entire time.
In 1832, a famous philosopher left very specific instructions for his own corpse.
His name was Jeremy Bentham, and he wanted to be useful even after death.
First, his body was to be dissected in public, for science!
His doctor lectured over the corpse while a thunderstorm shook the building.
Next, his skeleton was padded out, dressed in his own clothes, and seated in his own chair.
Legend says he had carried his future glass eyes in his pocket for years.
But the preserved head came out dark, dried and shrivelled!
So a French artist sculpted him a nicer one out of wax.
The real head was placed on the floor of the case, right between his feet!
In 1975, students from a rival college stole it and demanded a hundred pounds for charity.
In 2013, he was wheeled into a university council meeting as a surprise guest.
And today, he's still sitting in that London university, in his own clothes, watching everyone walk by!
